text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German Bund futures, defying some dealers' forecasts, vaulted across the key 97.00 level in late trading, managing to shrug off the effects from a slightly weaker U.S. market. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 97.15, up 0.31 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - British gilt futures closed unchanged from Tuesday's levels after marking time for most of the day pending publication of the U.S. Federal Reserve Beige Book. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 106-20/32, up 03/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French September bond futures posted a late rally, driven by short covering, to leave the contract within a whisker of the 30-month high reached earlier in the session. The September notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 124.24 up 0.34 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ended another strong session confirming a solidity not many in the market would have bet on just a few days ago, traders said. The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 116.78 up 0.27 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened lower with a fresh reminder of Federal Reserve policy makers' fears that rising labour costs could set off a gradual rise in inflation. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-10/32, up 04/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.12 percent.

JAPAN - December Japanese Goverment Bonds (JGB) ended in Tokyo higher but off the day's best levels some sales that corrected its rapid advance. Dec renewed its year's high in mid afternoon trade, hitting a high of 121.60. In after hours trading the September future on LIFFE was trading at 121.27, up 0.07 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Issuance was slower compared with Tuesday's flood, but dollar deals continued to surface. France Telecom launched a $400 million five-year Eurobond at 15 b.p. over Treasuries. Deutsche Bank set a $250 million December 1998 bond flat to Treasuries. Canadian dollars, yen and marks were also active. South Africa's upcoming mark Eurobond is likely to have a seven-year maturity, officials said.
